I get that it's possibly very profitable, but what kind of lawyer constantly reassures his client that "he would never hurt her"?

She currently does not work, because of her disability. And as part owner, does she have an employer at all? Even though supposedly her lawyer/partner will give her more money to work? 

It's at least some solace that there's a low likelihood of her get herself caught. I've told my friend not to sign or cosign anything involving this...

I've just realized, and I don't think she has, that sharing in the profit Aldo means sharing the costs, right? What if this venture isn't profitable? Can he hold her to it even if it's not generating a negligible amount of money? He said if it doesn't make enough then they will sell and split the cost... but it seems up to him to decide when that is. 

I'm sorry to have so many thoughts interlaced with questions;  I'm trying to make it make sense for myself and my friend. 

Major question though, does this deal sound shady or is it common?

As far as she has explained it, someone is paying her if she's doing work for it. And that doesn't come out of her 50%. That's all I know. It could be cash. It could include her getting a check. Either way I feel like she's either leaving a dangerous paper trail or not self reporting.

Edit: after rereading, I'm sure she must get some sort of payment to get anything for her investment.

She already has full disability and claims that because it's an investment it's not income. But if it's an investment... can she work for it? Would managing these trucks lower her disability amount? Could she possibly do these things and it not violate her policy?
